headline: Indian Markets End September With Worst Monthly Performance Since March Amid Global Headwinds

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Global rate hikes and rising crude oil prices sparked significant capital outflows
Persistent FII selling pressure weighed heavily on benchmark indices throughout September
Concerns over global economic headwinds led to the worst monthly performance since March
The market recorded its worst nine-month performance in 15 years due to sustained volatility
whatHappening: Nifty 50 and Sensex closed September with marginal losses after failing to hold intraday gains
The Textiles Ministry extended the RoSCTL scheme for apparel and made-ups exports until December 31
New Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam received official security clearance from the government
Market participants are watching for a potential bounce as Nifty tests support near the 22,600 level
summary: Indian markets concluded September with their worst monthly performance since March, driven by global headwinds and persistent FII outflows. The Nifty and Sensex remained volatile, closing near key support levels as the government provided security clearance for Air India's new CEO. Traders are now eyeing a potential bounce in October, supported by oversold conditions and the extension of textile export incentives.
